questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude for the Amplitude-Phase Form for Sine
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
7\operatorname{sin}⁡x+6\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
7\operatorname{sin}⁡x+6\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=7 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=6\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={7}^{2}+(6\sqrt{2})^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =49+72 \\ {R}^{2} & =121 \\ R & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

$$

$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ)
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=4 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0,$ what is the **exact** value of $ϕ?$

$ϕ=\operatorname{arctan}⁡($ 
{{field-1}} $)$
questions.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=5\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{5}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{5}{2} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{5}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: $\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=$
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{6} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}) \\ ϕ & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & =(\sqrt{6})^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =6+2 \\ {R}^{2} & =8 \\ R & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{30}^{∘})
$$

$$

$$

$$
\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{(\frac{3}{2})}{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\ ϕ & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}

$$
